subject: humanities
passage: Opera is usually sung in its original language, which many audience members do not understand. When a regional opera company in Canada began projecting English translations above the stage at the start of its 2013 season, its managers hoped the change would make performances in Italian, German, and French more welcoming. Arts administrator Grace Whitfield, who studied the company's ticket records, concludes that the change mattered mainly to newcomers: it drew a wave of first-time operagoers but did little to alter attendance among people who had attended the company's performances before.

data.title: Attendance at a Regional Opera Company by Season

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to support Whitfield's conclusion?

choices.A: After the translations were introduced in 2013, returning attendance rose by more than first-time attendance did.
choices.B: First-time attendance increased in every season shown, from 3,900 in 2011 to 7,300 in 2014.
choices.C: Returning attendees outnumbered first-time attendees by a wide margin in every season shown.
choices.D: From 2012 to 2013, first-time attendance rose by about 2,700, but returning attendance rose by only about 500.

explanation.why: Whitfield's conclusion has two parts tied to the moment the translations began in 2013: first-time attendance surged, but returning attendance barely changed. Support must compare the change in both series across that moment. From 2012 to 2013, first-time attendance rose from 4,100 to 6,800 (about 2,700), while returning attendance moved only from 21,100 to 21,600 (about 500).
explanation.A: Incorrect. From 2012 to 2013, first-time attendance rose about 2,700, while returning attendance rose about 500, so this reverses the data.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is true, but it covers first-time attendees only, and the rise from 2011 to 2012 came before the translations began.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is true, but which group was larger says nothing about how each responded to the translations.
explanation.D: Correct. It compares both groups across the 2013 change and shows a large jump for newcomers and little change for returning attendees.
